flagged.evidence: Step 4.1 asserts "Z*:=\limsup_mZ_m is \mathcal F^0_{T+}-measurable, equals Z almost surely, and as an a.s. class lies in L^2(\mathcal F^0_T) because \mathcal F^0_{T+}\subseteq\mathcal F^0_T". The inclusion is backwards: the item's dependency def-natural-and-usual-augmented-brownian-filtrations defines \mathcal F^0_{t+}:=\bigcap_{u>t}\mathcal F^0_u, and (\mathcal F^0_t) is increasing, so \mathcal F^0_T\subseteq\mathcal F^0_{T+} (that definition's clause (d) keeps the four families distinct and records \mathcal F^0_{0+}\neq\mathcal F^0_0 in the canonical realization). The completion fact actually needed - that \mathcal F_T is contained, modulo null sets, in \sigma(\mathcal F^0_T\cup\mathcal N), so that the \mathcal F_T-measurable Z has an \mathcal F^0_T-measurable a.s. representative and step 3.1's E[Z1_A]=0 for A\in\mathcal F^0_T forces Z=0 - is neither proved nor cited anywhere in the item (it needs downward martingale convergence to \mathcal F^0_{T+} plus the restarted Blumenthal/strong-Markov step). Moreover \limsup_mZ_m is only \bigvee_m\mathcal F^0_{T+1/m}=\mathcal F^0_{T+1}-measurable as defined. Hence the L^2 clause of the theorem is not established by the item as written; the statement itself (the standard Brownian representation theorem) is true.

Step 3.1 reads "Consequently $E\sum_{n\ge1}2^na_n^2=\sum_{n\ge1}2^nEa_n^2\le\sum_{n\ge1}2^{4-3n}<\infty$ by monotone convergence for the nonnegative series" and closes with the bracket "[F7, step 2.1]". The item's [F7] is "If $X_n\to X$ in $L^2(P)$ then $E|X_n-X|\le\|X_n-X\|_2\to0$, and conditional expectations are $L^1$-contractive", which contains no monotone-convergence statement; the monotone-convergence fact used is the item's [F4] ("If a sequence $0\le Z_n\uparrow Z$ of nonnegative random variables increases pointwise, then $E Z_n\uparrow E Z"). The identity asserted is correct once [F4] is cited; the citation points at the wrong fact.

[F7] defines "the stopping time $\rho_c:=\inf\{t:\max(|X_t|,|Y_t|,\int_0^t|b^X|,\int_0^t|b^Y|,\int_0^t\xi^2,\int_0^t\eta^2)\ge c\}\wedge T$" and then claims "$\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely as $c\to\infty$". Since $\rho_c\le T$ for every $c$ by construction, the sequence cannot tend to $\infty$. What steps 1.1 and 6.1 actually use ("by step 1.1 the identity holds on $\{\rho_c\ge T\}$ for each $c$, and $\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely, so the identity holds almost surely") is $\rho_c\uparrow T$ a.s., which does follow from the finite, continuous functionals named in the same sentence; as written the exhaustion premise of step 6.1 is a false claim.

[F7]: "For $c>0$ put $\rho_c:=\inf\{t:\max(|X_t|,\int_0^t|b|,\int_0^t\sigma^2)\ge c\}\wedge T$. ... and $\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely as $c\to\infty$ because $X$ is continuous and $\int|b|,\int\sigma^2$ are finite and continuous in the upper limit almost surely." Because $\rho_c\le T$, the sequence cannot go to $\infty$; the correct statement is $\rho_c\uparrow T$ a.s. Step 6.1's removal of the localization ("the identity has now been proved on each event $\{\rho_c\ge T\}$ ...; since $\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely, the identity holds almost surely") cites the false version.

[F7]: "For $c>0$ put $\rho_c:=\inf\{t:\max(|X_t|,\sum_i\int_0^t|b^i|,\sum_{i,k}\int_0^t(\sigma^{ik})^2)\ge c\}\wedge T$. ... and $\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely as $c\to\infty$." Since $\rho_c\le T$ identically, the claim is false; step 6.1 ("the identity holds on each $\{\rho_c\ge T\}$, and $\rho_c\uparrow\infty$ almost surely, so it holds almost surely") rests on it. The needed exhaustion of $\{\rho_c\ge T\}$ follows from $\rho_c\uparrow T$ a.s., i.e. from the a.s. finiteness of the capped functionals.

The Source notes still say: "The proof here packages the extension as an application of the characterization clause of the localized integral, with the localizing sequence $\rho_k=\tau\wedge\tau_k$." The proof on disk uses $\rho_k:=\tau_k$ (step 2.1: "the canonical sequence $\rho_k:=\tau_k$ is nondecreasing with $\rho_k\uparrow\infty$ almost surely"), so the note misdescribes the current proof; more importantly $\tau\wedge\tau_k\uparrow\tau$, not $\infty$, whenever $\tau<\infty$, and clause 3 of thm-localized-ito-integral requires a localizing sequence with $\rho_k\uparrow\infty$, so the sequence named in the note could not license the application it attributes to the proof. This is the surviving half of the very defect the batch reader repaired in steps 2.1/4.1.

Clause 2 reads: "If $\tau_U:=\inf\{t\ge0:(t,B_t)\notin U\}$ and $E\int_0^t|\nabla f|^2(s,B_s)1_{[0,\tau_U)}(s)\,ds<\infty$ for a given $t\ge0$, then $f(t,B_t)-f(0,0)=\int_0^t\sum_k\partial_{x_k}f(s,B_s)\,dB^k_s$". Since $f$ is defined only on the open set $U$, on the event $\{\tau_U<t\}$ (of positive probability for typical $U$, e.g. $U$ bounded in space) neither $f(t,B_t)$ nor the integrands $\partial_{x_k}f(s,B_s)$ for $s>\tau_U$ exist; the displayed integrand also drops the truncation $1_{[0,\tau_U)}$ that the clause's own hypothesis and clause 1 (which keeps $1_{[0,\tau_K]}$) use, and the proof only establishes the identity "on $[0,\tau_U)" (step 4.1). The correct display is $f(t\wedge\tau_U,B_{t\wedge\tau_U})-f(0,0)=\int_0^t1_{[0,\tau_U)}(s)\sum_k\partial_{x_k}f(s,B_s)\,dB^k_s$.
